figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. a) Simpliﬁed models depicting the types of biosynthetic pathways observed in natural oligomeric biosynthesis as well as representative
metabolites and enzymes.[12] (i) and (iv) represent two or more metabolites produced by separate biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), then undergo
an enzymatic or nonenzymatic heteromerization to give the ﬁnal natural product, respectively. (ii) represents two or more distinct metabolites from
the same BGC, then undergo an enzymatic reaction to give the ﬁnal natural product. (iii) and (v) represent two or more identical metabolites from
the same BGC, then undergo an enzymatic or nonenzymatic reaction to give the ﬁnal natural product, respectively. “Me 1′′, metabolite 1; “Me 2′′,
metabolite 2; “Me”, identical metabolite. The enzyme names are rendered with green. b) Representative meroaspochalasins from A. ﬂavipes. U,
subunit. c) Mimic total synthesis of meroaspochalasins 1–5 by two individual groups.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Conﬁrmation of the ﬂas and epi clusters and the function of major biosynthetic genes in the two clusters. a) Organization and deduced
function of the ﬂas and epi clusters. Aspo, gene cluster in A. ﬂavipes KLA03 for 6 biosynthesis; cluster A, gene cluster in A. terreus for azasperpyranone
A biosynthesis. b) LC-MS analysis of the metabolite proﬁle of the mutant strains. Extracted ion chromatography (EIC) traces were monitored at m/z
580.2910 and 564.2961 [M+H]+ for mAPO dimers 1–4 and 29–32, respectively; m/z 977.5164 [M+H]+ for trimer 5; m/z 400.2488 [M+H]+ for
aspochalasin monomers 7 and 11; m/z 181.0501 and 165.0554 [M+H-H2O]+ for polyketides 21 and 26, respectively. Polyketide lactone 27 possesses a
[M+H]+ ion at m/z 181.0501. The asterisk indicates an unknown isomer of 5. c) The structures of the compounds that were marked in the metabolite
proﬁle analysis (listed in detail in Table S1).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. a) In vitro biochemical characterization of the EpiD function with 23, 24, 25, and 33 as substrates. b,d) The key distance in the average
structure of binding mode A and the key distance in the average structure of the umbrella window with dis ﬁxed in 2.9 Å (binding mode B),
respectively. The carbon atoms of protein, ﬂavipin, and NADPH are rendered with green, cyan, and magenta, respectively; the black dashed lines
indicate hydrogen bonds, and the orange dashed lines indicate the distance associated with the reaction; BM-A and BM-B, binding mode A and B,
respectively. c) Free energy proﬁle of the shifting of 7-CHO toward the active site. dis, distance. e) The proposed biosynthetic pathway of benzo
hemiacetals 21 and 26. The intermediates framed by dashed lines are hypothetical; the previously veriﬁed substrates and reactions are rendered grey.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Elucidating the nonenzymatic polymerization in the formation of mAPOs in A. ﬂavipes. a) Incubation experiment of 26 in the ultraﬁltrate of
the epiA strain fermentation, in which the mycelium and proteins are removed (i–ii). Incubation of 7 with 21 or 50 in PDB medium at 30 °C for 8 h
(iii–v). b) LC-MS analysis of 26 after incubation in H2O and H218O for 48 h on positive and negative ion modes. c) Proposed nonenzymatic
mechanism of mAPOs formation in A. ﬂavipes. The intermediates framed by dashed lines are hypothetical.
